subject: docs/coop/artifacts/distribution-core-inventory-contract.v3.json

shouldFix.title: The duplicate-digest alias exception introduces an undefined second edge relation.
evidence: inventorySchema.dependencyGraph calls the inventory a directed requires-graph, and graphRules.edgeRelation defines only consumer-to-dependency 'requires' edges, their direction, and cycle refusal.

graphRules.nodeIdentity nevertheless allows duplicate sha256 values at different paths when the second is an 'explicit alias edge', then states that this artifact does not mint that edge. No field defines alias-edge direction, endpoints, whether the second path remains a node, or how alias edges affect roots, cycle detection, layers, and closure traversal.

Because node identity is already {path, sha256}, equal bytes at distinct paths are distinct identities; the unexplained exception also fails to distinguish a true path alias from two independent files with identical content.
shouldFix.impact: A populated successor can either reject a repeated digest, admit it by labeling an undefined alias edge, or count its second path differently in roots and closure. Those outcomes all fit parts of the text, so edge direction and graph membership remain non-deterministic despite the claimed repair.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Either remove the exception and make duplicate-sha256-under-different-path an unconditional failure, or define a closed alias relation: direction, endpoint/node representation, eligibility, layer assignment, root/cycle/closure treatment, and the distinction between a filesystem alias and independent equal-content files. If aliases are future work, reserve them to a named owner and make them unavailable to successors under this version.
